KEY MESSAGE 1...Periodic showers and thunderstorms are expected through 
Thursday. Some storms will be severe later this afternoon and evening.

W'erly to WNW'erly mid/upper-level flow near 40 to 60 knots and
embedded shortwave disturbances affect our region through 
Thursday. At the surface, our CWA resides within a warm and very
humid sector originating over the Gulf before a cold front 
sweeps E'ward through Western and Central NY between about 2 AM 
and 9 AM EDT Thursday morning. This warm and very humid air mass
will contribute to periods of heavy rainfall with showers and 
storms (more details below). Behind the cold front, an extensive
high pressure ridge associated with a cooler and drier air mass
begins to build from northern ON and vicinity. High temperatures
are expected to reach mainly the mid 70's to mid 80's this 
afternoon and be followed by overnight lows in the 60's around 
daybreak Thursday. Highs should reach the 70's to 80F late 
Thursday afternoon.

As of 2:50 PM EDT, a broken line of showers and thunderstorms, 
including supercells, had already developed over southern ON, 
along a pre-front surface trough axis. Periodic and organized 
showers and thunderstorms amidst moderate to strong deep-layer 
bulk shear are expected today through Thursday as at least weak 
to moderate CAPE, including elevated CAPE, is released by the 
following: moist isentropic ascent ahead of shortwave trough 
axes; low-level convergence/moist ascent along surface trough 
axes attendant to the shortwave troughs and along the cold 
front; downshear outflow boundaries interacting favorably with 
ambient low-level vertical wind shear. Of greatest concern is 
the aforementioned storms that have developed over southern ON. 
These storms are expected to grow upscale into a QLCS consisting
of multicells, including bowing segments, and supercells as the
storms persist generally ESE'ward and impact our CWA late this 
afternoon, and especially this evening, and encounter a pre-
storm environment that includes moderate to strong boundary 
layer CAPE. Strong to damaging straight-line wind gusts are 
expected as the storms encounter steep low-level lapse rates and
moderate to strong DCAPE stemming from diurnal convective 
mixing of the boundary layer through this late afternoon and 
then limited nocturnal cooling in the warm/moist sector boundary
layer this evening into tonight. Sporadic severe hail is 
possible due to mid-level lapse rates near 7C/km contributing to
large MUCAPE in the hail growth zone, but rich low-level 
moisture contributing to unfavorably-high ambient atmospheric 
melting levels near 11kft AGL should curb the severe hail 
threat, at least somewhat. A few tornadoes are possible with 
mesocyclones and mesovortices, and a strong tornado cannot be 
ruled out since low-level winds veering and strengthening 
significantly with height should yield surface-based ESRH near 
150-300 m2/s2 amidst favorably-low mixed layer LCL's. Localized 
flash flooding is possible through tonight, especially where 
showers and storms manage to train along any outflow boundaries 
that manage to become oriented largely parallel to the W'erly to
WNW'erly mean mid-level flow.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Quieter weather, overall, expected Thursday night 
through Saturday.

The surface high pressure ridge continues to build from 
northern ON, and vicinity and humidity at the surface and aloft
continues to decrease gradually, Thursday night through 
Saturday. However, northwesterly flow aloft and embedded 
shortwave troughs will continue to impact our region through 
Friday before the ridge aloft begins to build from the west 
Friday night through Saturday. Moist isentropic ascent ahead of 
the shortwave trough axes and low-level convergence/moist ascent
along surface trough axes attendant to the shortwaves may 
release weak, yet sufficient instability, including elevated 
CAPE, to generate isolated showers and thunderstorms Thursday 
night through Friday. Current odds favor fair weather Friday 
night through Saturday due to stabilizing subsidence 
accompanying the ridge at the surface and aloft. Lows should 
reach the mid 50's to mid 60's around daybreak Friday and mainly
the upper 40's to near 60F around daybreak Saturday as the 
cooler air mass associated with the ridge continues to 
overspread Western and Central NY. Late afternoon highs should 
reach the 70's on Friday and the mid 60's to mid 70's on 
Saturday. Note: partial clearing, the cooler air mass, lingering
low-level moisture, and weak surface winds should yield steam 
fog in the river and lake valleys east of Lake Ontario, in the 
Finger Lakes, and in the Western Southern Tier around daybreak 
Friday and Saturday, respectively.
